instruction.text: Choose the correct concept for the definition.

atoms.a: A branch of computer science dealing with the development of systems that are able to imitate human intelligence. They can perform tasks that would normally require human beings.
A sequence of rules a computer has to follow to solve a task. It helps the AI model with the recognition of certain patterns and decision-making.
A branch of AI that enables algorithms to learn from experience, recognise patterns and make decisions without being explicitly taught.
AI models consisting of complex neural networks trained by extensive data sets. They are designed to understand and generate natural language.
Describes the systematic discrimination in the outputs of the AI model due to insufficient or unrepresentative training data and causes faulty or discriminatory results.
A type of AI system that can create data similar to what it was trained with.
Certain safety measures that are implemented in AI systems to ensure a safe use in various ways.
The instruction users put into the language model to solve a task or receive a certain answer. Its quality determines the quality of the output.
Negative term for AI generated low-quality media content flooding the internet.
A set of commands integrated to an AI model that determines its behaviour, tone, role and rules prior to the user's prompt.
AI-generated content, for example pictures or videos, that appears deceptively realistic.

instruction.text: Categorise the aspects below into advantages and disadvantages of AI.
Match the quote to the right category.

atoms.a:
“AI is not here to replace the workforce, but to liberate it. By automating the mundane, we unlock a historic wave of human creativity and global economic growth. It’s the ultimate upgrade for civilization.”

— Dr. Asish Vanroy, tech entrepreneur

“The greatest danger of artificial intelligence is not a terminator-like rebellion, but our own slow surrender. If we outsource our thinking to algorithms, we lose the very cognitive friction that makes us human.”

— Prof. Ellen Romanov, cognitive scientist

“We don't need fewer AI tools in classrooms; we need better AI literacy. Giving students AI without teaching them how to question its outputs is like giving someone a sports car without a driving licence.”

— Michael Dallas, school council

“Once AI surpasses human intelligence, we become the second-smartest species on Earth. Historically, the less intelligent species rarely fares well when a dominant power takes over. We are building our own eclipse.”

— Dr. Dalal Dersim, AI-safety researcher and author

“Artificial intelligence knows no borders. If governments fail to implement strict, unified ethical regulations today, tomorrow’s democratic processes will be entirely engineered by corporate algorithms.”

— Sara Mansoor, UN Secretary-General’s Envoy on Technology

“Think of AI as a bicycle for the mind. It doesn't ride itself, but it allows the human user to travel ten times faster and farther in daily tasks than ever before.”

— Linus Brown, software engineer
